not_applicable_because: the main text, Methods and legends give no cut-off and never define the classes abnormal, intermediate and normal; the paper's own seven evidence categories are cut on the VarCall Bayes factor or posterior probability, which the cited score table does not carry

quotes.text: A VarCall model<sup>8</sup>, a class of Bayesian hierarchical model that embeds a Gaussian two-component mixture model, was applied to the position-adjusted LFC values of D14 and D0 ratios. Each variant was assigned an indicator of pathogenicity status: deterministically if known and probabilistically if unknown. In detail, nonsense variants were assumed to be pathogenic, whereas silent variants, except for variants with known or predicted splice effects, were assumed to be benign.

quotes.where: Methods, 'VarCall model for assessment of evidence of pathogenicity'
quotes.text: A prior probability of pathogenicity of 0.2 for variants in the DNA-binding region was used based on a predicted frequency of 0.23 for pathogenic variants in this region by AlphaMissense. Using the MCMC output, the Bayes factor in favour of pathogenicity for each variant was computed. The thresholds for the Bayes factor based on strength of evidence of pathogenicity or benign level (P<sub>Strong</sub>, P<sub>Moderate</sub> or P<sub>Supporting</sub>, VUS, B<sub>Strong</sub>, B<sub>Moderate</sub> or B<sub>Supporting</sub>) were derived from the Bayesian interpretation of the ACMG–AMP guidelines<sup>23</sup>. Full details of the analysis are available in the Supplementary Methods.

The combined benign (B<sub>Strong</sub>, B<sub>Moderate</sub> and B<sub>Supporting</sub>) and combined pathogenic (P<sub>Strong</sub>, P<sub>Moderate</sub> and P<sub>Supporting</sub>) categories accounted for 81.6% and 16.6% of variants, respectively, with 1.8% remaining as VUS.
